title: Stay in Your Lane
coreMove: Build from your own expertise and conviction instead of borrowing another speaker's surface style.
sourcePressure: The source closes on authenticity, originality, real enthusiasm, and lived voice. It includes passion and mood-contagion support through Matthieu Ricard, Larry Smith, Melissa Cardon, Jill Bolte Taylor, and Howard Friedman while warning against imitation.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version says be yourself. The useful version says build a prepared, structured talk from real expertise, conviction, and voice rather than copying someone else's recognizable surface.

sourceAnchors.name: Matthieu Ricard
sourceAnchors.detail: the source connects Ricard to authentic motivation, joy, calm, and audience connection
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Matthieu Ricard helps show that authenticity can sound calm when the motive is real.

sourceAnchors.name: Larry Smith
sourceAnchors.detail: the source uses Smith as support for urgency and conviction around meaningful work
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Larry Smith's urgency matters because it comes from a concern he cannot treat lightly.

sourceAnchors.name: Howard Friedman mood-contagion work
sourceAnchors.detail: the source says mood-contagion work summarized through Friedman supports the claim that genuine positive energy spreads to the audience
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Friedman's mood-contagion support belongs where the prose explains why borrowed enthusiasm feels thinner than real energy.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.audience: a postdoc tempted to copy a famous lab director's theatrical style
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether her own careful fieldwork gets buried under borrowed swagger
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she deletes the imitation opener and begins with the muddy notebook page that only her field season could have produced
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a rain-warped field notebook opened under a hotel desk lamp

exampleSpecs.audience: a technical founder pitching hospital buyers after watching too many famous product launches
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether buyers trust his actual knowledge of their workflow or see a borrowed performance
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he removes the slick reveal, opens with the nurse's handoff bottleneck he personally observed, and lets his own domain knowledge carry the pitch
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a worn nurse handoff clipboard beside a closed laptop

exampleSpecs.audience: a principal addressing students after copying a viral commencement clip
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether students hear a trend or the actual adult who knows their hallway
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after a student mutters that she sounds like a video, she rewrites the assembly around the lost-and-found table and the habit she sees every morning
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a lost-and-found table piled with hoodies beside a gym microphone

exampleSpecs.audience: a distiller leading visitors through a tasting after imitating a luxury-brand script
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether visitors remember the actual craft or a pasted-on prestige voice
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he drops the velvet vocabulary, names the dent in the copper still, and explains the repair his father taught him
exampleSpecs.firstImage: warm copper reflecting a shallow dent near a distillery gauge

exampleSpecs.audience: a senior defender training new attorneys who admire a courtroom celebrity
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether new lawyers copy aggression instead of building credibility from client knowledge
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she asks which opening sounds stronger, then reveals that the quieter version wins because it contains the client's exact timeline and no borrowed outrage
exampleSpecs.firstImage: two opening statements printed on opposite sides of a legal pad

exampleSpecs.audience: a conductor speaking to donors after trying to sound like a famous maestro
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether donors hear grand borrowed language or the conductor's actual reason for the community program
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he cuts the grand phrasing, lifts the student's repaired viola case, and speaks from the program he actually runs every Tuesday
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a scuffed viola case resting against a rehearsal-room chair

skillTargets: distinguish authenticity from lack of preparation
choose details rooted in lived expertise
evaluate whether originality serves credibility and audience transfer

tryThisNowSpec: Look at your opening minute and cross out any move borrowed from a speaker you admire; replace it with one detail only your work, room, or lived experience could supply.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
